_meta.honest_yield_note: 2 confirmed notes is the expected result: Sundara is epic adventure narrative, not a Vedic ritual text. The 2 confirmed notes are both genuine theological anchors (mārutātmaja ← Maruts as sons of Rudra; varuṇālaya ← Varuṇa as lord of cosmic waters). All other stems are either too common (agni 460 Vedic hits, indra 1161 hits, sūrya 199 hits) or the Vedic verse does not illuminate the Sundara context.

rejected.reason: Agni in Sundara is used as a simile for brightness or as a divine name in a list (V.13.65). The Vedic Agni-hymns (RV 1.1 etc.) are the canonical source for Agni, but the Sundara uses (flames, fire similes) do not invoke Vedic ritual theology — they are stock epic imagery. No specific verse-level parallel illuminates a Sundara passage beyond what is already obvious. The Agni-ordeal of Sītā occurs in Book VI (Yuddhakāṇḍa), not in Sundara. Reject.

Indra appears in Sundara as comparative epithet (suras, vāsava, puruhūta) or in lists of divine names (V.13.65). 1161 Vedic hits makes any intersection non-distinctive. No specific Vedic hymn illuminates Sundara's use. Reject.
Sūrya/sun appears as brightness simile in Sundara. Too widespread in both texts. No specific shared formula. Reject.

Pāvaka (Purifier = Agni) at RV 1.64.12 occurs in the Marut-hymn (already cited for mārutātmaja note). In Sundara, pāvaka is used for fiery brightness (V.1.19-20 burning rocks, V.1.176 thunderbolts). No Vedic verse specifically illuminates these Sundara passages beyond the general Agni identification. Reject.

Samudra (ocean) in RV is primarily used for the cosmic gathering of waters, not as Varuṇa's abode specifically. The varuṇālaya note captures the Vedic ocean theology better. Additional samudra hits add nothing. Reject.

Satyavant ('possessing truth') appears in RV in formulaic invocations. In Sundara it is an epithet of Rāma. The connection is terminological only — Manu 4.138 (satya as dharma) already covers this via the dharmashastra cluster. Reject as duplicate covered by better parallel.

rejected.src: RV (68 hits but mostly viśvāyu compound)
rejected.reason: The vAyu stem in the RV source index is dominated by viśvāyu ('all-life') in Agni contexts, not Vāyu-the-wind-god. The actual Vāyu-god hymns (RV 1.134 etc.) are not in our selected RV books. The Vedic anchor for Hanumān's wind-father is better captured by the Marut note (mārutātmaja ← rudrasya sūnu). Reject as subsumed.

RV 10.154.4-5 mentions tapasvataḥ ('those possessed of tapas') in a hymn about the dead joining the fathers. Sundara tapasvin (ascetics, Sītā as tapasvinī) is in a living-world context unrelated to the death ritual. Register mismatch. Reject.

AV 11.5 is indeed the great tapas-hymn (tapasā brahma jajñe). Sundara uses tapas as 'austerity power' (Sītā's celibacy, Hanumān's discipline). The connection is real but too general — tapas in this sense pervades all Sanskrit literature. No specific verse-level parallel makes this note more illuminating than what the reader already knows. Reject as underdetermined.
